models.name: SpliceAI
models.notes: Calls splice donors and acceptors at single-base resolution from 10 kb of flanking sequence. Repository archived by Illumina; models are CC BY-NC 4.0.

papers.title: Predicting Splicing from Primary Sequence with Deep Learning

input_requirements.note: For the tracked model, assay-specific predictions do not require a user-supplied cell-state or chromatin profile.

models.name: AlphaGenome
models.notes: Reads 1 Mb at base resolution across every major readout, including splice junctions and contact maps. Served through an API; weights released in 2026 behind a gated Hugging Face licence.

papers.title: Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome

training_data.stage: Supervised training on functional genomics measurements
training_data.summary: Human and mouse reference sequences paired with molecular readouts across many tissues and cell types.
training_data.assays: RNA-seq, CAGE, PRO-cap, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq, TF and histone ChIP-seq, and genomic contact maps
training_data.coverage: Human and mouse; hundreds of cell types and tissues.
training_data.size: A single total for training examples or assay datasets has not been curated; the authors report hundreds of cell types and tissues.
training_data.split: Four genomic cross-validation folds; fold-specific models use held-out intervals for validation and testing. The all-folds model uses all folds.
training_data.overlap: Benchmark-specific overlap has not been assessed; check the model version and fold for each evaluation.

references.label: AlphaGenome model card and training data

input_requirements.note: For the tracked model, assay-specific predictions do not require a user-supplied cell-state or chromatin profile.

models.name: Enformer
models.notes: Adds transformer attention to reach distal enhancers; the default baseline for most later work. The Hugging Face id is the PyTorch port of the official weights (enformer-pytorch).

papers.title: Effective gene expression prediction from sequence by integrating long-range interactions

training_data.stage: Supervised human and mouse training, followed by human fine-tuning
training_data.summary: Human and mouse reference sequences paired with chromatin and transcription measurements from the Basenji2 dataset.
training_data.sources: Basenji2 dataset; ENCODE, Roadmap Epigenomics and FANTOM
training_data.assays: TF and histone ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq and CAGE
training_data.coverage: Human and mouse genomes; multiple tissues and cell types.
training_data.size: 34,021 human and 29,295 mouse training sequence examples; 5,313 human and 1,643 mouse assay tracks.
training_data.split: Separate training, validation and test genomic sequences; the paper reports 2,213 human and 2,209 mouse validation examples, and 1,937 human and 2,017 mouse test examples.
training_data.overlap: Benchmark-specific overlap has not been assessed.

input_requirements.note: For the tracked model, assay-specific predictions do not require a user-supplied cell-state or chromatin profile.

models.notes: Predicts RNA-seq coverage at 32 bp, so one model covers transcription, splicing and polyadenylation. The Hugging Face ids are the PyTorch port of the official weights (johahi/borzoi-pytorch).

papers.title: Predicting RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence as a unifying model of gene regulation

training_data.stage: Supervised training on genomic assay tracks
training_data.summary: Human and mouse genomic sequences paired with RNA-seq coverage and other functional genomics tracks.

training_data.size: The RNA-seq component includes 866 human and 279 mouse ENCODE datasets; these are not counts of all training tracks or sequence examples.
training_data.split: Four genomic cross-validation folds; training, validation and test intervals vary by fold.
training_data.overlap: Benchmark-specific overlap has not been assessed.
